Definition
A very common use for the multimeter is to measure voltage.
INTRODUCTIONM
Voltage measurements tell a lot about the operation of a circuit.
For example, if the voltage measurement in this circuit is zero, you can be sure it is not working properly.
Throughout this course you will use voltage measurements to determine the operating condition of circuits. This is an overlay page.

VOLTAGE MEASUREMENT CHECKLIST
If you know the approximate value of voltage you will measure, set the range switch to a setting just higher than that value. Enter the discussion text here.
For example, if the measured voltage is expected to be 50 volts, set the range switch to 60. This setting lets you measure any value between 0 and 60 volts. This is an overlay page.

If the voltage value is unknown, set the range switch to the highest possible setting. Doing this will ensure that you do not cause the meter needle to deflect full scale or off the scale. This is commonly referred to as "pegging the meter".

DISCUSSION
Let's look at the cautions that must be observed when measuring voltage.
It is most important to know that voltage is dangerous when not used properly. Always use caution. This is an overlay page.
Following these simple rules can keep you safe from harm.
DEFINITION
REMOVE ALL JEWELRY - Jewelry makes a good conductor. Allowing metal jewelry to come in contact with a circuit can KILL. cond line here.
TOUCH CIRCUITS WITH TEST LEADS ONLY - Touching a circuit with your finger can be dangerous. Use the test leads, they are insulated to prevent shock.
DEFINITION
KNOW THE CIRCUIT'S VOLTAGE LEVEL - Know the approximate voltage level of the circuit you measure. If you don't know, don't measure the circuit.

Your meter has two test leads, one black and one red. The black lead is called the ground or negative lead.
If we use a flashlight battery as an example, the black lead is
placed on the negative end of the battery.
The red lead is called the positive lead and is placed at a point
that is more positive than the negative lead.
Notice, that the meter indicates the voltage of the battery.
